title: Mitigating Replay Attacks in TLS 1.3 Early Data
explanation: TLS 1.3 introduces 0-RTT handshakes to eliminate round-trip delays for returning clients. The client sends application data alongside its first handshake message. This early data relies on previously negotiated preshared keys. However, attackers can intercept and replay these initial unauthenticated packets to the server. If the server processes non-idempotent HTTP requests in early data, state changes occur multiple times. To prevent replay attacks, servers must implement single-use ticket keys or maintain a bloom filter of recent connection identifiers. Alternatively, applications must restrict 0-RTT to strictly idempotent GET requests. Failing to isolate early data exposes backend APIs to duplicate transactions. Proper TLS configuration requires explicit white-listing of safe application endpoints.
takeaway: Restrict TLS 0-RTT early data processing strictly to safe, idempotent HTTP methods to block replay attack vectors on backend services.
author: Muhammad Junaeid
